# [Baseline] - MAC - D - Azure Files Cloud Kerberos

Gives the Mac a Kerberos ticket for the Entra Cloud Kerberos realm, so that an SMB share on Azure Files opens without the user signing in again.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | macOS |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | Microsoft Learn — Enable Microsoft Entra Kerberos authentication for Azure Files on macOS with Platform SSO (preview), and the Entra guide for Kerberos SSO in Platform SSO; settingDefinitionIds verified against the settings catalog definitions |
| File | [`Baseline_MAC_D_Azure_Files_Cloud_Kerberos.json`](Baseline_MAC_D_Azure_Files_Cloud_Kerberos.json) |

> Belongs with [Baseline] - MAC - D - Platform SSO and does nothing without that policy: the cloud TGT is issued by Platform SSO; this profile only tells Apple's Kerberos extension which realm goes with it and that it may use that TGT (`usePlatformSSOTGT`). `performKerberosOnly` keeps the extension away from password expiry checks, password synchronisation and the home directory path — those belong to Platform SSO, not here.
>
> A second policy alongside Platform SSO and not an extension of it: the settings catalog has two separate forms for `com.apple.extensiblesso`, the Platform SSO form (`com.apple.extensiblesso_com.apple.extensiblesso`) and the Kerberos form this policy uses (`com.apple.extensiblesso_com.apple.extensiblesso-kerberos_kerberos`). Each Kerberos realm is one such form, with its own `Realm` and its own `Hosts`. On the Mac those profiles are installed side by side and macOS merges the payloads; check-scope.js therefore deliberately does not report that overlap on Apple as a conflict.
>
> The tenant id is in the `preferredKDCs` URL as `%OrganizationId%`, the same construction as in the OneDrive KFM and Teams policies: CIPP replaces that token at deployment with the tenant's customerId (see Get-CIPPTextReplacement in CIPP-API); `%tenantid%` does the same. If you deploy with IntuneBackupAndRestore instead of CIPP, that replacement does not happen and you have to fill in the id by hand.
>
> On the tenant side, four things must be in place before this profile achieves anything: Entra Kerberos enabled on the storage account, admin consent on the associated service principal, MFA off for that storage account's Entra app, and share-level permissions on the share itself. If the file share already exists, the identifier URI of that app registration is `CIFS/<account>.file.core.windows.net` — in capitals. macOS only mounts on `cifs/` in lower case; Microsoft provides `updateappmanifestazurefiles.ps1` for this in azure-files-samples. New shares do not have that problem.
>
> **A storage account that already has another identity source is ruled out.** If the account uses Microsoft Entra Domain Services — for example because an AVD environment depends on it — then Entra Kerberos and AD DS are greyed out in the portal with "Another access method is already configured". A storage account can only have one. On a Mac with a valid cloud TGT, `kgetcred cifs/<account>.file.core.windows.net@KERBEROS.MICROSOFTONLINE.COM` then returns AADSTS700016 — there is no app registration for the file service, so there is nothing to issue. Entra DS is not an alternative route to the same goal either: Platform SSO only issues `tgt_cloud` (Entra Kerberos) and `tgt_ad` (on-premises AD via Cloud Kerberos Trust), and Entra DS is neither. Changing the identity source affects all existing traffic to those shares, including the file- and folder-level permissions set with Entra DS identities; see "Change the identity source for Azure file shares" at Microsoft. The full diagnosis is in shellscripts/macos/README.md.
>
> **What is needed to deploy this.** A storage account with Entra Kerberos as its identity source. If the existing account uses something else and cannot be switched, a **second storage account** is needed with Entra Kerberos as its identity source — the two can coexist; the restriction applies per account, not per tenant. This profile does not need to change for that: `Hosts` covers every storage account with `.windows.net`, and only the mount script in `shellscripts/macos/` names an account. If that is not worth the effort, the honest conclusion is that SMB is the wrong vehicle here and the data belongs in SharePoint, with `automountteamsites` from the settings catalog — that works on both platforms without Kerberos and without VPN.
>
> The on-premises AD side would be a second policy of this form, with its own realm and its own domain name in `Hosts`. It is not included here — this baseline assumes cloud-only devices. If it is added, the on-prem profile should be deployed first and this one after it, in that order. The TGT mapping itself can be controlled with `custom_tgt_setting` in the extension data of the Platform SSO policy (Company Portal 2508+); the default value 0 maps both the on-prem and the cloud TGT, which is why that policy does not need to change for this profile.
>
> For Platform SSO profiles Microsoft says "assign to users, not to devices". This baseline keeps macOS profiles on device groups, same as the existing Platform SSO policy. As long as the policy is in phase 3 this makes no practical difference: it is created and not assigned.
>
> Verify after deployment: `app-sso platform -s` in Terminal must show a ticket with `ticketKeyPath` = `tgt_cloud`, and `nc -vz <account>.file.core.windows.net 445` must be open. That the Kerberos extension's menu bar extra reports "Not signed in" is normal and does not mean it is not working.
